records.source: וּבִשְׁנַת֙ שְׁמֹנֶ֣ה עֶשְׂרֵ֔ה לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־נְבָ֑ט מָלַ֥ךְ אֲבִיָּ֖ם עַל־יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And in [the] year eighteen of the king Jeroboam son of Nebat reigned Abijam over Judah.
pieces: In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijam became king over Judah.

L.1: And in [the] eighteenth year of King Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijam reigned over Judah.

R.1: Abijam became king of Judah. It was the eighteenth year that Jeroboam son of Nebat had been king of Israel.

decisions.choice: dated by the reign of the king in the other kingdom
decisions.reason: From here on, Kings dates the start of each reign by the year of the king ruling in the other kingdom, Israel or Judah. This is the first time it does so. The formula then gives the length of the reign, the king's mother (for Judah) and a verdict on the king (verses 2-3, 9-11, 25-26, 33-34).

decisions.choice: reigned: began to reign, became king
decisions.reason: The verb means "to be king" or "to become king". With a date it marks the start of the reign, as in the accession formula of 14:21.

decisions.choice: Abijam: the same king 2 Chronicles 13:1-2 calls Abijah
decisions.reason: Kings calls him Abijam throughout (verses 1, 7, 8), and Chronicles calls him Abijah (2 Chronicles 13:1-23). Abijah means "my father is Yahweh"; Abijam may be another form of the name, or a different spelling of it that came about in copying. Some ancient copies and translations have a form closer to Abijah here. The record keeps Abijam, the form this book uses.

decisions.choice: two sentences, the date second
decisions.reason: Readable splits the formula into two sentences, as these books allow, and names Israel so the reader knows which kingdom Jeroboam ruled.

records.heading: Abijam king of Judah

records.source: שָׁלֹ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ מַעֲכָ֖ה בַּת־אֲבִישָׁלֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: Three years he reigned in Jerusalem, and [the] name of his mother [was] Maacah daughter of Abishalom.
pieces: He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.

L.2: Three years he reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother [was] Maacah daughter of Abishalom.

R.2: He ruled in Jerusalem for three years. His mother was Maacah, the daughter of Abishalom.

decisions.choice: three years: counted in part-years
decisions.reason: Abijam began in Jeroboam's eighteenth year (verse 1) and Asa in his twentieth (verse 9). Kings counts a part of a year as a year, so the reign may have been little more than two full years.

decisions.choice: his mother's name: the queen mother named in the formula
decisions.reason: For the kings of Judah the formula names the king's mother (14:21), because the queen mother held a position of her own at court (verse 13).

decisions.choice: Maacah daughter of Abishalom: probably Absalom son of David; "daughter" may mean granddaughter
decisions.reason: Abishalom is a fuller form of Absalom, and 2 Chronicles 11:20-22 says Rehoboam married Maacah daughter of Absalom and made her son Abijah his heir. 2 Chronicles 13:2 instead names Abijah's mother "Micaiah daughter of Uriel of Gibeah". Since Absalom's only daughter we know of was Tamar (2 Samuel 14:27), Maacah may have been his granddaughter, as "daughter" can mean a female descendant. The text says "daughter", and every level keeps it.

decisions.choice: He reigned three years; He ruled ... for three years
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable start with the subject, as English does; Literal keeps the Hebrew order, which puts the number first.

records.source: וַיֵּ֕לֶךְ בְּכָל־חַטֹּ֥אות אָבִ֖יו אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֣ה לְפָנָ֑יו וְלֹא־הָיָ֨ה לְבָב֤וֹ שָׁלֵם֙ עִם־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֔יו כִּלְבַ֖ב דָּוִ֥ד אָבִֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he walked in all [the] sins of his father which he had done before him, and not was his heart whole with Yahweh his God like [the] heart of David his father.
pieces: He walked in all the sins his father had committed before him, and his heart was not wholly given to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God, as the heart of his ancestor David had been.

L.3: And he walked in all the sins of his father that he had done before him, and his heart was not whole with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God, like the heart of David his father.

R.3: He committed all the same sins his father had committed before him. He was not completely loyal to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God, as his ancestor David had been.

decisions.choice: walked in all the sins of his father: lived by the same sins as Rehoboam
decisions.reason: To walk in something is to live by it. Rehoboam's reign had allowed high places, standing stones, Asherah poles and shrine prostitutes throughout Judah (14:22-24), and Abijam carried on the same ways.

decisions.choice: his heart was not whole with Yahweh: his loyalty to Yahweh was divided
decisions.reason: The word means whole, complete or at peace. A heart that is whole with Yahweh belongs to him undivided. The same words were said of Solomon in his old age, when his heart was turned toward other gods (11:4). Asa's heart, by contrast, is whole with Yahweh (verse 14).

decisions.choice: David his father: his ancestor David
decisions.reason: David was Abijam's great-grandfather. "Father" in Hebrew also means a forefather, and the books of Kings measure each king of Judah against David (verses 5, 11).

decisions.choice: wholly given to
decisions.reason: Balanced turns "whole with" into "wholly given to", which keeps the picture of an undivided heart. Readable says what the idiom means: "completely loyal".

decisions.choice: his ancestor David
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "ancestor" for "father" here (m3), as they do wherever David is called the father of a later king; Literal keeps "father".

records.source: כִּ֚י לְמַ֣עַן דָּוִ֔ד נָתַן֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהָ֥יו ל֛וֹ נִ֖יר בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לְהָקִ֤ים אֶת־בְּנוֹ֙ אַחֲרָ֔יו וּֽלְהַעֲמִ֖יד אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: But for [the] sake of David gave Yahweh his God to him a lamp in Jerusalem, to raise up his son after him and to establish Jerusalem,
pieces: Yet for David's sake {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God gave him a lamp in Jerusalem, setting up his son to rule after him and keeping Jerusalem secure,

L.4: But for the sake of David, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God gave him a lamp in Jerusalem, by raising up his son after him and by establishing Jerusalem,

R.4: But because of David, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God kept a lamp burning for him in Jerusalem. He made Abijam's son king after him and kept Jerusalem safe.

decisions.choice: but: in contrast to Abijam's sins
decisions.reason: The word sets what Yahweh did against what Abijam deserved (verse 3). Yahweh did not end David's line because of Abijam's sins.

decisions.choice: for David's sake: because of Yahweh's promise to David
decisions.reason: Yahweh had promised David that his house and his kingdom would last (2 Samuel 7:12-16), and he had said he would keep one tribe for Solomon's son for David's sake (11:12-13, 32).

decisions.choice: a lamp: a descendant who keeps the family line alive
decisions.reason: A lamp left burning in a house is a sign that someone still lives there. Yahweh had promised that David would always have a lamp before him in Jerusalem (11:36). The verse explains the lamp: a son to reign after Abijam, and a city kept standing.

decisions.choice: to raise up ... and to establish: the two ways the lamp was given
decisions.reason: The two verbs say how Yahweh gave the lamp: by raising up Abijam's son as king and by keeping Jerusalem firm. The sentence goes on in verse 5 with the reason.

decisions.choice: kept a lamp burning ... made Abijam's son king
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture of the lamp but makes it a lamp kept burning, and names Abijam so that "his son" is clear. It ends the sentence here and starts verse 5 afresh.

records.source: אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֥ה דָוִ֛ד אֶת־הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹֽא־סָ֞ר מִכֹּ֣ל אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֗הוּ כֹּ֚ל יְמֵ֣י חַיָּ֔יו רַ֕ק בִּדְבַ֖ר אוּרִיָּ֥ה הַחִתִּֽי׃
records.gloss: because did David the right in [the] eyes of Yahweh, and not he turned aside from all that he commanded him all [the] days of his life, only in [the] matter of Uriah the Hittite.
pieces: because David had done what was right in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and had not turned aside from anything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded him as long as he lived, except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.

L.5: because David did the right in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and did not turn aside from anything that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded him all the days of his life, except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.

R.5: This was because David had done what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was right. All his life he had never turned away from anything God commanded him, except in what he did to Uriah the Hittite.

decisions.choice: did what was right in Yahweh's eyes: the verdict for a faithful king
decisions.reason: This is the good verdict of the regnal formula, the opposite of "did what was evil in Yahweh's eyes" (14:22). David is the measure for the kings after him (verse 11).

decisions.choice: except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite: David's adultery with Bathsheba and the killing of her husband
decisions.reason: David took Bathsheba, Uriah's wife, and had Uriah killed in battle (2 Samuel 11). Nathan's rebuke followed (2 Samuel 12:1-14). The narrator names it as the one great exception to David's faithfulness.

decisions.choice: God commanded him
decisions.reason: Readable says "God" in place of the pronoun, so the reader does not take "he" for David.

records.source: וּמִלְחָמָ֨ה הָיְתָ֧ה בֵין־רְחַבְעָ֛ם וּבֵ֥ין יָרָבְעָ֖ם כָּל־יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And war was between Rehoboam and between Jeroboam all [the] days of his life.
pieces: There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of Abijam's life.

L.6: And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of his life.

R.6: The war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam went on as long as Abijam lived.

decisions.choice: the verse repeats 14:30 inside Abijam's reign
decisions.reason: These words are almost the same as 14:30, which closes Rehoboam's reign, and some ancient Greek copies do not have the verse here. It may have been copied here from 14:30. The Hebrew text has it, and it fits with verse 7: the war that began under Rehoboam went on under his son.

decisions.choice: his life: Abijam's lifetime
decisions.reason: Since the verse stands in Abijam's reign, "his" most likely means Abijam: the war between the two kingdoms that started under Rehoboam lasted all through Abijam's life too (verse 7). It could also mean Rehoboam's life, as in 14:30.

decisions.choice: Abijam's life
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Abijam for "his" (m2), since a bare "his" after two names would leave the reader guessing. Literal keeps "his".

records.source: וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֤י אֲבִיָּם֙ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה הֲלֽוֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה וּמִלְחָמָ֥ה הָיְתָ֛ה בֵּ֥ין אֲבִיָּ֖ם וּבֵ֥ין יָרָבְעָֽם׃
records.gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Abijam and all that he did, [are] not they written on [the] book of [the] matters of the days of [the] kings of Judah? And war was between Abijam and between Jeroboam.
pieces: The rest of the acts of Abijam, and all that he did, are written in the Book of the History of the Kings of Judah. There was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.

L.7: And the rest of the matters of Abijam and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah? And there was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.

R.7: Everything else Abijam did is written in the history of the kings of Judah. There was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah: a royal record the writer could consult
decisions.reason: As at 14:29, the writer sends the reader to a fuller written record of Judah's kings, now lost. The question "are they not written ...?" means "they are written".

decisions.choice: war between Abijam and Jeroboam: told in 2 Chronicles 13
decisions.reason: Chronicles tells of a battle in this war in which Abijah defeated Jeroboam (2 Chronicles 13:2-20).

decisions.choice: a statement in place of the question
decisions.reason: As in the sources formula throughout these books, Balanced and Readable state as a fact what the Hebrew asks as a question; Literal keeps the question.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב אֲבִיָּם֙ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקְבְּר֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֑ד וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אָסָ֥א בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ
records.gloss: And lay down Abijam with his fathers, and they buried him in [the] city of David, and reigned Asa his son in his place.
pieces: Then Abijam rested with his ancestors and was buried in the City of David. His son Asa became king in his place.

L.8: And Abijam lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the City of David, and Asa his son reigned in his place.

R.8: Then Abijam died and was buried in the City of David. His son Asa became king after him.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers: died
decisions.reason: The death formula of Kings, as at 2:10 and 14:31.

decisions.choice: Asa his son: the next king of Judah
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 13:23 reports the same succession. On Asa's mother, see verse 10.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers / rested with his ancestors / died
decisions.reason: The death formula is worded the same way at each level throughout Kings. Balanced and Readable say "was buried" because the Hebrew "they buried him" names no one in particular.

records.source: וּבִשְׁנַ֣ת עֶשְׂרִ֔ים לְיָרָבְעָ֖ם מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מָלַ֥ךְ אָסָ֖א מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And in [the] year twenty of Jeroboam king of Israel reigned Asa king of Judah.
pieces: In the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa became king of Judah.

L.9: And in [the] twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa king of Judah reigned.

R.9: Asa became king of Judah in the twentieth year that Jeroboam was king of Israel.

decisions.choice: reigned: became king
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, the verb with a date marks the start of the reign.

decisions.choice: became king of Judah
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "Asa king of Judah reigned"; Balanced and Readable fold the title into the verb, as the accession formula does at these levels.

records.heading: Asa king of Judah

records.source: וְאַרְבָּעִ֤ים וְאַחַת֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ מַעֲכָ֖ה בַּת־אֲבִישָׁלֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And forty and one year[s] he reigned in Jerusalem, and [the] name of his mother [was] Maacah daughter of Abishalom.
pieces: He reigned forty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.

L.10: And forty-one years he reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother [was] Maacah daughter of Abishalom.

R.10: He ruled in Jerusalem for forty-one years. His mother was Maacah, the daughter of Abishalom.

decisions.choice: his mother: probably his grandmother, who stayed queen mother
decisions.reason: Verse 2 gives the same name, Maacah daughter of Abishalom, for the mother of Abijam, Asa's father. "Mother" here most likely means grandmother: Maacah kept her place as queen mother into Asa's reign until he removed her (verse 13). Another possibility is that Asa was Abijam's brother rather than his son, but verse 8 calls him Abijam's son. Every level keeps "mother", as the text has it.

decisions.choice: He reigned forty-one years; He ruled ... for forty-one years
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

records.source: וַיַּ֧עַשׂ אָסָ֛א הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּדָוִ֖ד אָבִֽיו׃
records.gloss: And did Asa the right in [the] eyes of Yahweh, like David his father.
pieces: Asa did what was right in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, as his ancestor David had done.

L.11: And Asa did the right in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, like David his father.

R.11: Asa did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was right, as his ancestor David had done.

decisions.choice: did what was right in Yahweh's eyes: the good verdict
decisions.reason: Asa is the first king after Solomon to receive the good verdict, and he is compared to David (verse 5). Verses 12-15 say what he did, and verse 14 adds the one thing he did not do.

decisions.choice: did the right in [the] eyes of / did what was right in the sight of / did what the LORD said was right
decisions.reason: The good verdict is worded like the evil one (14:22), at each level the same way throughout the book. "Ancestor" as in verse 3.

records.source: וַיַּעֲבֵ֥ר הַקְּדֵשִׁ֖ים מִן־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיָּ֨סַר֙ אֶת־כָּל־הַגִּלֻּלִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשׂ֖וּ אֲבֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he made pass away the male shrine prostitutes from the land, and he removed all the idols which had made his fathers.
pieces: He drove the male shrine prostitutes out of the land and removed all the idols his ancestors had made.

L.12: And he made the male cult prostitutes pass away from the land, and he removed all the idols that his fathers had made.

R.12: He drove out of the land the men who served as prostitutes at the shrines. He got rid of all the idols his ancestors had made.

decisions.choice: male shrine prostitutes: men who served at the shrines of other gods
decisions.reason: The men attached to the shrines whom Rehoboam's Judah had allowed, as at 14:24, where the note explains the word and why its sexual sense is not certain.

decisions.choice: idols: a scornful word for idols
decisions.reason: The word is used only for idols, and always with contempt; it may come from a word for dung (Ezekiel uses it often). It names images of other gods that earlier kings had allowed.

decisions.choice: his fathers: the kings before him
decisions.reason: Rehoboam and Abijam, and before them Solomon, who built shrines for foreign gods (11:7-8).

decisions.choice: the men who served as prostitutes at the shrines
decisions.reason: Each level words the term as at 14:24; Readable explains it with a short description.

records.source: וְגַ֣ם׀אֶת־מַעֲכָ֣ה אִמּ֗וֹ וַיְסִרֶ֨הָ֙ מִגְּבִירָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־עָשְׂתָ֥ה מִפְלֶ֖צֶת לָאֲשֵׁרָ֑ה וַיִּכְרֹ֤ת אָסָא֙ אֶת־מִפְלַצְתָּ֔הּ וַיִּשְׂרֹ֖ף בְּנַ֥חַל קִדְרֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And also Maacah his mother, and he removed her from [being] queen mother, because she had made a horrid thing for Asherah; and cut down Asa her horrid thing and burned [it] in [the] valley of Kidron.
pieces: He even deposed his mother Maacah as queen mother, because she had made a horrid image for Asherah. Asa cut down her image and burned it in the Kidron Valley.

L.13: And also Maacah his mother: he removed her from [being] queen mother, because she had made a horrid thing for Asherah; and Asa cut down her horrid thing and burned [it] in the valley of Kidron.

R.13: He even took away the title of queen mother from Maacah, his mother, because she had made a disgusting idol to worship the goddess Asherah. Asa cut the idol down and burned it in the Kidron Valley.

decisions.choice: queen mother: an office at the royal court
decisions.reason: The word means "great lady". In Judah the king's mother held a recognized place of honor and influence (2:19; 2 Kings 10:13; Jeremiah 13:18). Asa took that position away from Maacah. On whether she was his mother or his grandmother, see verse 10.

decisions.choice: a horrid thing: an object meant to cause horror or disgust
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root meaning to shudder, and it is found only here and in the parallel, 2 Chronicles 15:16. It names something made for worship that the narrator calls horrifying; what it looked like is not known. The verb "cut down" suggests it was made of wood or stood up like a pole.

decisions.choice: Asherah: the goddess, or a wooden pole standing for her
decisions.reason: Asherah was a Canaanite goddess, and the same word names the wooden poles set up in her honor (14:15, 23). Here Maacah's object is made "for Asherah", so the word most likely names the goddess.

decisions.choice: the valley of Kidron: the valley on the east side of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The word is used for a valley with a stream that runs only in the rainy season. Kings who cleansed Judah of idols burned or threw them away there (2 Kings 23:4, 6, 12).

decisions.choice: horrid image (Balanced); disgusting idol (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "horrid thing"; Balanced and Readable call it an image or idol, since it was made for worship (m2).

decisions.choice: to worship the goddess Asherah
decisions.reason: Readable says who Asherah was (m3).

records.source: וְהַבָּמ֖וֹת לֹא־סָ֑רוּ רַ֣ק לְבַב־אָסָ֗א הָיָ֥ה שָׁלֵ֛ם עִם־יְהוָ֖ה כָּל־יָמָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And the high places not were removed; only [the] heart of Asa was whole with Yahweh all his days.
pieces: The high places, however, were not taken away. Even so, Asa's heart was wholly given to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} all his life.

L.14: But the high places were not removed; only, the heart of Asa was whole with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} all his days.

R.14: But the hilltop shrines were not removed. Even so, Asa was completely loyal to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} all his life.

decisions.choice: the high places were not removed: the reservation in the good verdict
decisions.reason: The high places were local places of worship (3:2). Kings counts it against even the good kings of Judah that they left them standing (22:44; 2 Kings 12:4; 14:4), until Hezekiah and Josiah removed them (2 Kings 18:4; 23:8). The verb does not say who failed to remove them; 2 Chronicles 14:4 says Asa removed high places from the towns of Judah, and 15:17 that they were not removed from Israel.

decisions.choice: his heart was whole with Yahweh: his loyalty to Yahweh was undivided
decisions.reason: The same words as in verse 3, now said in his favor: unlike Abijam, Asa served Yahweh with an undivided heart, even though the high places remained.

decisions.choice: high places (Literal, Balanced); hilltop shrines (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for this word in these books.

decisions.choice: Even so
decisions.reason: The word "only" here limits the first clause: the high places stayed, but that did not make Asa's heart divided. Balanced and Readable say "even so"; "wholly given to" and "completely loyal" as in verse 3.

records.source: וַיָּבֵא֙ אֶת־קָדְשֵׁ֣י אָבִ֔יו וְקָדְשֵׁ֖י בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה כֶּ֥סֶף וְזָהָ֖ב וְכֵלִֽים׃
records.gloss: And he brought [the] holy things of his father and his holy things [into the] house of Yahweh: silver and gold and vessels.
pieces: He brought into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the gifts his father had dedicated and the gifts he himself had dedicated: silver, gold and utensils.

L.15: And he brought the holy things of his father and his holy things [into the] house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: silver and gold and vessels.

R.15: He brought into the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the gifts of silver and gold and other objects that his father and he himself had set apart for God.

decisions.choice: his own holy things
alternatives: the holy things of his father and the holy things of the house of Yahweh
decisions.reason: The letters written in the Hebrew text read "and his holy things", that is, the things Asa himself had dedicated. The vowels and the reading in the margin give "and the holy things of", joining the words to "the house of Yahweh". The record follows the written form, which agrees with 2 Chronicles 15:18, "his father's holy things and his own holy things".

decisions.choice: holy things: gifts dedicated to Yahweh
decisions.reason: Things declared holy belonged to Yahweh and were kept in the temple's treasuries, often silver and gold taken in war (7:51; 2 Samuel 8:11). Abijam's are perhaps from his war with Jeroboam (2 Chronicles 13:16-19).

decisions.choice: his holy things; [into the]
decisions.reason: Literal has "his" from the written form (m1). "Into the" is bracketed because the Hebrew has no preposition: the house is the place the gifts were brought to.

decisions.choice: temple; set apart for God
decisions.reason: Readable calls the house of the LORD the temple, and explains "holy things" as gifts set apart for God (m2).

records.source: וּמִלְחָמָ֨ה הָיְתָ֜ה בֵּ֣ין אָסָ֗א וּבֵ֛ין בַּעְשָׁ֥א מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כָּל־יְמֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And war was between Asa and between Baasha king of Israel all their days.
pieces: There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel as long as they both lived.

L.16: And there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.

R.16: Asa and Baasha king of Israel were at war with each other as long as they both were king.

decisions.choice: Baasha king of Israel: named here before his reign is told
decisions.reason: Baasha's rise to power is told in verses 27-28 and his reign in verse 33 and chapter 16. The writer finishes Asa's story first, and the war with Baasha belongs to it (verses 17-22).

decisions.choice: all their days: the whole time both were alive and reigning
decisions.reason: Baasha reigned twenty-four years (verse 33), all within Asa's forty-one (verse 10). The war was not always open fighting; verses 17-22 tell its main episode.

decisions.choice: as long as they both were king
decisions.reason: Readable says what "all their days" means here (m2).

records.source: וַיַּ֨עַל בַּעְשָׁ֤א מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ עַל־יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיִּ֖בֶן אֶת־הָרָמָ֑ה לְבִלְתִּ֗י תֵּ֚ת יֹצֵ֣א וָבָ֔א לְאָסָ֖א מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And went up Baasha king of Israel against Judah, and he built the Ramah, to not allow [one] going out and coming in to Asa king of Judah.
pieces: Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and fortified Ramah, to keep anyone from going out or coming in to Asa king of Judah.

L.17: And Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah, and he built Ramah, so as not to allow [anyone] going out or coming in to Asa king of Judah.

R.17: Baasha king of Israel marched against Judah and built up the town of Ramah into a fortress. He wanted to stop anyone from traveling to or from the land of Asa king of Judah.

decisions.choice: built: fortified
decisions.reason: Ramah was already a town; Baasha built it up as a fortress. The same verb is used for Asa's work at Geba and Mizpah (verse 22).

decisions.choice: Ramah: a town in Benjamin on the main road north of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Ramah lay about five miles north of Jerusalem, on the road through the hill country. A fortress there could close the road to Jerusalem from the north and press on Judah's border.

decisions.choice: going out and coming in: all traffic to and from Asa's kingdom
decisions.reason: The pair of words takes in all movement in both directions: travelers, trade, and perhaps people from the north who wanted to go over to Judah (2 Chronicles 15:9).

decisions.choice: fortified (Balanced); built up ... into a fortress (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the building was for (m1); Literal keeps "built".

decisions.choice: traveling to or from the land of Asa
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (m3) and makes clear that it means Asa's kingdom, not Asa's person.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֣ח אָ֠סָא אֶת־כָּל־הַכֶּ֨סֶף וְהַזָּהָ֜ב הַֽנּוֹתָרִ֣ים׀בְּאוֹצְר֣וֹת בֵּית־יְהוָ֗ה וְאֶת־אֽוֹצְרוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֖ם בְּיַד־עֲבָדָ֑יו וַיִּשְׁלָחֵ֞ם הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָסָ֗א אֶל־בֶּן־הֲ֠דַד בֶּן־טַבְרִמֹּ֤ן בֶּן־חֶזְיוֹן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֔ם הַיֹּשֵׁ֥ב בְּדַמֶּ֖שֶׂק לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And took Asa all the silver and the gold remaining in [the] treasuries of [the] house of Yahweh and [the] treasuries of [the] house of the king, and he gave them into [the] hand of his servants, and sent them the king Asa to Ben-hadad son of Tabrimmon son of Hezion king of Aram, the [one] dwelling in Damascus, saying,
pieces: Then Asa took all the silver and gold that was left in the treasuries of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the treasuries of the king's palace, and handed it over to his officials. King Asa sent them to Ben-hadad son of Tabrimmon, son of Hezion, the king of Aram, who ruled in Damascus, with this message:

L.18: And Asa took all the silver and the gold that remained in the treasuries of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the treasuries of the house of the king, and he gave them into the hand of his servants, and King Asa sent them to Ben-hadad son of Tabrimmon son of Hezion, king of Aram, who lived in Damascus, saying,

R.18: So Asa took all the silver and gold that was left in the treasure rooms of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and of the royal palace. He gave it to his officials and sent them to Ben-hadad, king of Aram, who ruled from Damascus. Ben-hadad was the son of Tabrimmon and grandson of Hezion. Asa sent him this message:

decisions.choice: the silver and gold that remained: what was left after Shishak's raid
decisions.reason: Shishak king of Egypt had carried off the treasures of the temple and of the palace in Rehoboam's fifth year (14:25-26). Asa now empties what was left or had been added since (verse 15).

decisions.choice: Ben-hadad king of Aram, who lived in Damascus
decisions.reason: Aram was the kingdom of the Arameans north and east of Israel, with its capital at Damascus (11:23-25). Ben-hadad means "son of Hadad", the storm god of the Arameans, and several kings of Damascus bore the name (20:1; 2 Kings 13:3). "Dwelling in" a city, said of a king, means ruling from it.

decisions.choice: son of Tabrimmon son of Hezion: his father and grandfather
decisions.reason: The second "son of" names Ben-hadad's grandfather. Hezion may be the Rezon who founded the kingdom of Damascus in Solomon's day (11:23-24), though this is not certain.

decisions.choice: servants (Literal); officials (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: These are the king's court officials, sent as envoys, as the wording of these books has it for a king's servants.

decisions.choice: Ben-hadad's ancestry in a sentence of its own
decisions.reason: Readable moves the list of names into a separate sentence and says "grandson" for the second "son of" (m3).

records.source: בְּרִית֙ בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵינֶ֔ךָ בֵּ֥ין אָבִ֖י וּבֵ֣ין אָבִ֑יךָ הִנֵּה֩ שָׁלַ֨חְתִּֽי לְךָ֥ שֹׁ֨חַד֙ כֶּ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֔ב לֵ֣ךְ הָפֵ֗רָה אֶת־בְּרִֽיתְךָ֙ אֶת־בַּעְשָׁ֣א מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְיַעֲלֶ֖ה מֵעָלָֽי׃
records.gloss: "A covenant [is] between me and between you, between my father and between your father. Look, I have sent to you a bribe of silver and gold. Go, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, and he will go up from on me."
pieces: "Let there be a treaty between you and me, as there was between my father and your father. I am sending you a bribe of silver and gold. Go and break off your treaty with Baasha king of Israel, and he will withdraw from me."

L.19: "[There is] a treaty between me and you, between my father and your father. Look, I have sent you a bribe of silver and gold. Go, break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will go up from me."

R.19: "Let us make a treaty with each other, as our fathers did. I am sending you silver and gold as a bribe. Break off your treaty with Baasha king of Israel. Then he will pull his army back from my land."

decisions.choice: a treaty between me and you: a request for a treaty like the one their fathers had
alternatives: there is a treaty between me and you, as between my father and your father
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no verb: "a treaty between me and you, between my father and your father". It may state that a treaty already stands, or ask that one be made on the model of the fathers' treaty. Since Ben-hadad has a treaty with Baasha that he must break, Asa is most likely asking him to change sides and renew the old alliance with Judah.

decisions.choice: bribe: a payment to change someone's decision
decisions.reason: The word is used elsewhere for a bribe that bends a judge (Exodus 23:8; Deuteronomy 16:19). Here it is a payment to make Ben-hadad break his word to Baasha. The word does not mean a friendly gift; it marks the deal as a buying of loyalty, paid for with the temple's treasures (verse 18).

decisions.choice: he will go up from on me: he will withdraw his forces from my territory
decisions.reason: To go up from someone is to break off an attack and withdraw (2 Kings 12:19; Jeremiah 21:2). Asa wants Baasha to leave Ramah and Judah's border (verse 17).

decisions.choice: as our fathers did
decisions.reason: Readable puts "between my father and your father" into a shorter phrase with the same meaning.

decisions.choice: pull his army back from my land
decisions.reason: Readable says what "go up from me" means (m3).

records.source: וַיִּשְׁמַ֨ע בֶּן־הֲדַ֜ד אֶל־הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָסָ֗א וַ֠יִּשְׁלַח אֶת־שָׂרֵ֨י הַחֲיָלִ֤ים אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ֙ עַל־עָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת־עִיּ֣וֹן וְאֶת־דָּ֔ן וְאֵ֖ת אָבֵ֣ל בֵּֽית־מַעֲכָ֑ה וְאֵת֙ כָּל־כִּנְר֔וֹת עַ֖ל כָּל־אֶ֥רֶץ נַפְתָּלִֽי׃
records.gloss: And listened Ben-hadad to the king Asa, and he sent [the] commanders of the forces which [were] his against [the] cities of Israel, and he struck Ijon and Dan and Abel-beth-maacah and all Chinneroth, with all [the] land of Naphtali.
pieces: Ben-hadad agreed with King Asa and sent the commanders of his forces out against the cities of Israel. He conquered Ijon, Dan, Abel-beth-maacah and all Chinneroth, as well as all the land of Naphtali.

L.20: And Ben-hadad listened to King Asa, and he sent the commanders of the forces that [were] his against the cities of Israel, and he struck Ijon and Dan and Abel-beth-maacah and all Chinneroth, with all the land of Naphtali.

R.20: Ben-hadad agreed to what King Asa asked. He sent the commanders of his armies to attack the towns of Israel. They defeated Ijon, Dan, Abel-beth-maacah and the whole area around Lake Chinneroth, and all the land of the tribe of Naphtali.

decisions.choice: listened to: agreed to
decisions.reason: To listen to someone's request is to agree to it and act on it.

decisions.choice: struck: attacked and defeated
decisions.reason: The verb means to strike; used of towns it means to attack and conquer them.

decisions.choice: Ijon, Dan, Abel-beth-maacah, Chinneroth, Naphtali: the far north of Israel
decisions.reason: These towns lay on the road south from Aram into Israel, near the sources of the Jordan. Chinneroth is the region by the lake later called the Sea of Galilee (Joshua 11:2; 12:3), and Naphtali the tribal land west of it. Dan was one of the places where Jeroboam had set up a golden calf (12:29). The same towns fell to Assyria later (2 Kings 15:29).

decisions.choice: agreed with, conquered (Balanced); agreed to, defeated (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "listened" and "struck" mean here (m1, m2).

decisions.choice: the whole area around Lake Chinneroth; the tribe of Naphtali
decisions.reason: Readable explains that Chinneroth is a region by a lake and Naphtali a tribe's land (m3).

records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ כִּשְׁמֹ֣עַ בַּעְשָׁ֔א וַיֶּחְדַּ֕ל מִבְּנ֖וֹת אֶת־הָֽרָמָ֑ה וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב בְּתִרְצָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was as heard Baasha, and he stopped from building the Ramah, and he stayed in Tirzah.
pieces: When Baasha heard about it, he stopped building Ramah and stayed in Tirzah.

L.21: And it happened, when Baasha heard [of it], that he stopped building Ramah, and he stayed in Tirzah.

R.21: When Baasha heard about this, he stopped work on Ramah and stayed in his capital, Tirzah.

decisions.choice: Tirzah: the capital of Israel at this time
decisions.reason: Jeroboam had his residence at Tirzah (14:17), and Baasha and the kings after him reigned from there (verse 33; 16:8, 15, 23) until Omri built Samaria (16:24). Baasha pulled back from the border to his capital.

decisions.choice: heard: heard of Ben-hadad's attack
decisions.reason: The verb has no object; what Baasha heard is the news of verse 20.

decisions.choice: [of it]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the object English needs (m2).

decisions.choice: his capital, Tirzah
decisions.reason: Readable says what Tirzah was (m1).

records.source: וְהַמֶּ֨לֶךְ אָסָ֜א הִשְׁמִ֤יעַ אֶת־כָּל־יְהוּדָה֙ אֵ֣ין נָקִ֔י וַיִּשְׂא֞וּ אֶת־אַבְנֵ֤י הָֽרָמָה֙ וְאֶת־עֵצֶ֔יהָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּנָ֖ה בַּעְשָׁ֑א וַיִּ֤בֶן בָּם֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָסָ֔א אֶת־גֶּ֥בַע בִּנְיָמִ֖ן וְאֶת־הַמִּצְפָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And the king Asa summoned all Judah, none [was] exempt, and they carried away [the] stones of the Ramah and its timbers which had built Baasha, and built with them the king Asa Geba of Benjamin and the Mizpah.
pieces: Then King Asa called up all Judah, with no one exempt, and they carried away the stones and timber Baasha had used to build Ramah. With them King Asa fortified Geba of Benjamin and Mizpah.

L.22: And King Asa summoned all Judah, none [was] exempt, and they carried away the stones of Ramah and its timbers with which Baasha had built, and King Asa built with them Geba of Benjamin and Mizpah.

R.22: Then King Asa called out all the men of Judah. No one was excused. They carried away the stones and wood that Baasha had been using at Ramah. King Asa used them to build up the towns of Geba in Benjamin and Mizpah.

decisions.choice: summoned all Judah, none exempt: a call to forced labor that no one could avoid
decisions.reason: The verb means to make people hear, that is, to summon by public announcement. "None exempt" means every man was called to work, with no one released from it.

decisions.choice: Geba of Benjamin and Mizpah: border towns north of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Both towns lay on Judah's northern border, close to Ramah. By fortifying them Asa turned Baasha's materials into his own defense line. Jeremiah 41:9 mentions a cistern Asa made at Mizpah.

decisions.choice: all the men of Judah
decisions.reason: Readable says "men" because those called up for heavy building work were the men of Judah; the call itself is "all Judah".

decisions.choice: fortified (Balanced); build up (Readable)
decisions.reason: As with Ramah (verse 17), the building was a fortifying of existing towns.

records.source: וְיֶ֣תֶר כָּל־דִּבְרֵֽי־אָ֠סָא וְכָל־גְּב֨וּרָת֜וֹ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֗ה וְהֶֽעָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּנָ֔ה הֲלֹֽא־הֵ֣מָּה כְתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה רַ֚ק לְעֵ֣ת זִקְנָת֔וֹ חָלָ֖ה אֶת־רַגְלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And [the] rest of all [the] matters of Asa and all his might and all that he did and the cities which he built, [are] not they written on [the] book of [the] matters of the days of [the] kings of Judah? Only in [the] time of his old age he was diseased in his feet.
pieces: The rest of all the acts of Asa, all his might, all that he did and the cities he built, are written in the Book of the History of the Kings of Judah. But in his old age he had a disease in his feet.

L.23: And the rest of all the matters of Asa, and all his might, and all that he did, and the cities that he built, are they not written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah? Only, in the time of his old age he was diseased in his feet.

R.23: Everything else Asa did, his great deeds and the towns he built, is written in the history of the kings of Judah. But when he was old, he had a disease in his feet.

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah
decisions.reason: The sources formula, as in verse 7.

decisions.choice: his might: his strength and his mighty deeds
decisions.reason: The word means strength or valor, and in these formulas it covers a king's achievements in war (16:5, 27; 22:46).

decisions.choice: diseased in his feet: an illness of his feet, perhaps a euphemism
alternatives: he had a disease of the private parts
decisions.reason: The plain sense is a disease of the feet, which 2 Chronicles 16:12 calls severe and which grew worse until his death. Since "feet" is sometimes a polite word for the private parts (Isaiah 7:20; Ruth 3:4 is debated), some take it as a hidden way of naming a disease there. The record keeps "feet". The word "only" sets this against the praise before it: the one dark note at the end of a long reign.

decisions.choice: a statement in place of the question
decisions.reason: As in verse 7.

decisions.choice: his great deeds
decisions.reason: Readable says what "his might" refers to (m2).

records.source: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב אָסָא֙ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקָּבֵר֙ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֔יו בְּעִ֖יר דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יו וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ
records.gloss: And lay down Asa with his fathers, and he was buried with his fathers in [the] city of David his father, and reigned Jehoshaphat his son in his place.
pieces: Then Asa rested with his ancestors and was buried with them in the City of David his ancestor. His son Jehoshaphat became king in his place.

L.24: And Asa lay down with his fathers, and he was buried with his fathers in the City of David his father, and Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place.

R.24: Then Asa died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Jehoshaphat became king after him.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers: died
decisions.reason: The death formula, as in verse 8. Here the Hebrew also names his burial "with his fathers" in the royal tombs.

decisions.choice: Jehoshaphat his son
decisions.reason: Jehoshaphat's own reign is told in 22:41-51.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers / rested with his ancestors / died ... and was buried with his ancestors
decisions.reason: The death formula as in verse 8; Readable keeps the burial with his ancestors because the Hebrew names it. Readable leaves out "his ancestor" after David, since "the City of David" is a place name.

records.source: וְנָדָ֣ב בֶּן־יָרָבְעָ֗ם מָלַךְ֙ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בִּשְׁנַ֣ת שְׁתַּ֔יִם לְאָסָ֖א מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שְׁנָתָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And Nadab son of Jeroboam reigned over Israel in [the] year two of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel two years.
pieces: Nadab son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel two years.

L.25: And Nadab son of Jeroboam reigned over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel two years.

R.25: Nadab son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in the second year that Asa was king of Judah. He ruled Israel for two years.

decisions.choice: Nadab son of Jeroboam: the second king of Israel
decisions.reason: Jeroboam's death and Nadab's accession were reported at 14:20. The account of his reign follows the same formula as the kings of Judah, but without naming a queen mother.

decisions.choice: two years: counted in part-years
decisions.reason: Nadab began in Asa's second year and died in Asa's third (verse 28), so his two years were part of one year and part of the next, as in verse 2.

decisions.choice: became king
decisions.reason: The first verb marks the start of the reign (verse 1); the second, "reigned", gives its length.

records.heading: Nadab king of Israel

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ֙ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ אָבִ֔יו וּ֨בְחַטָּאת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶחֱטִ֖יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, and he walked in [the] way of his father and in his sin which he caused to sin Israel.
pieces: He did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and walked in the way of his father and in his sin, by which he had led Israel to sin.

L.26: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and he walked in the way of his father and in his sin that he made Israel sin.

R.26: He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil. He lived as his father had lived and kept on in the sin by which his father had led Israel into sin.

decisions.choice: did what was evil in Yahweh's eyes: the bad verdict
decisions.reason: The evil verdict of the regnal formula, as at 14:22. Every king of the northern kingdom receives it.

decisions.choice: his sin which he caused Israel to sin: Jeroboam's golden calves at Bethel and Dan
decisions.reason: The sin is Jeroboam's: the calves he set up at Bethel and Dan, with their priests and feasts, so that Israel would not go up to Jerusalem (12:26-33; 13:33-34; 14:16). The verb means to cause someone to sin: Jeroboam led the whole people into it. This phrase becomes the verdict on nearly every king of Israel after him.

decisions.choice: walked in the way of his father: lived as his father had
decisions.reason: To walk in someone's way is to follow his example.

decisions.choice: his sin that he made Israel sin / his sin, by which he had led Israel to sin / the sin by which his father had led Israel into sin
decisions.reason: The wording kept for this formula at each level throughout Kings (14:16). Readable names "his father" so it is clear whose sin it was (m2).

records.source: וַיִּקְשֹׁ֨ר עָלָ֜יו בַּעְשָׁ֤א בֶן־אֲחִיָּה֙ לְבֵ֣ית יִשָּׂשכָ֔ר וַיַּכֵּ֣הוּ בַעְשָׁ֔א בְּגִבְּת֖וֹן אֲשֶׁ֣ר לַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וְנָדָב֙ וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל צָרִ֖ים עַֽל־גִּבְּתֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And conspired against him Baasha son of Ahijah of [the] house of Issachar, and struck him Baasha at Gibbethon which [belonged] to the Philistines, and Nadab and all Israel [were] besieging Gibbethon.
pieces: Baasha son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, plotted against him and struck him down at Gibbethon, a town of the Philistines, while Nadab and all Israel were laying siege to Gibbethon.

L.27: And Baasha son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him, and Baasha struck him at Gibbethon, which [belonged] to the Philistines, while Nadab and all Israel were besieging Gibbethon.

R.27: Baasha son of Ahijah, from the tribe of Issachar, plotted against Nadab. Nadab and the whole army of Israel were attacking the Philistine town of Gibbethon, and there Baasha struck him down.

decisions.choice: Baasha son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar
decisions.reason: This Ahijah is not the prophet Ahijah of Shiloh, who came from Ephraim's territory (verse 29; 11:29). "House of Issachar" means the tribe of Issachar. Baasha was not of Jeroboam's family or tribe, and this is the first time a king of Israel is overthrown by a rival.

decisions.choice: Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines
decisions.reason: Gibbethon had been assigned to the tribe of Dan (Joshua 19:44; 21:23), but the Philistines held it. Israel was still fighting for it a generation later (16:15).

decisions.choice: struck him: struck him down, killed him
decisions.reason: Verse 28 says the same act plainly: Baasha killed him.

decisions.choice: the whole army of Israel
decisions.reason: "All Israel" besieging a town means Israel's army in the field; Readable says so.

decisions.choice: the siege told before the killing
decisions.reason: Readable tells the setting first and the killing after, so the sentences follow the order of events.

records.source: וַיְמִתֵ֣הוּ בַעְשָׁ֔א בִּשְׁנַ֣ת שָׁלֹ֔שׁ לְאָסָ֖א מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּמְלֹ֖ךְ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And killed him Baasha in [the] year three of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned in his place.
pieces: Baasha killed him in the third year of Asa king of Judah and became king in his place.

L.28: And Baasha killed him in the third year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned in his place.

R.28: Baasha killed Nadab in the third year that Asa was king of Judah, and he became king of Israel in Nadab's place.

decisions.choice: in the third year of Asa
decisions.reason: The date is the same as Baasha's accession in verse 33, which gives the formula for his reign.

decisions.choice: Nadab; king of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable names Nadab for the pronouns and says which kingdom Baasha now ruled.

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י כְמָלְכ֗וֹ הִכָּה֙ אֶת־כָּל־בֵּ֣ית יָרָבְעָ֔ם לֹֽא־הִשְׁאִ֧יר כָּל־נְשָׁמָ֛ה לְיָרָבְעָ֖ם עַד־הִשְׁמִד֑וֹ כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּיַד־עַבְדּ֖וֹ אֲחִיָּ֥ה הַשִּׁילֹנִֽי׃
records.gloss: And it was as he reigned, he struck all [the] house of Jeroboam; not he left any breathing [one] to Jeroboam until he had destroyed it, according to [the] word of Yahweh which he spoke by [the] hand of his servant Ahijah the Shilonite,
pieces: As soon as he became king, he struck down the whole house of Jeroboam. He did not leave Jeroboam a single living soul, but destroyed them all, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant Ahijah of Shiloh,

L.29: And it happened, as soon as he reigned, he struck all the house of Jeroboam; he did not leave to Jeroboam anyone breathing until he had destroyed it, according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke by the hand of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} slave Ahijah the Shilonite,

R.29: As soon as Baasha became king, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family. He did not leave a single one of them alive, but wiped out the whole family. This was what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said would happen, through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant the prophet Ahijah from Shiloh.

decisions.choice: according to the word of Yahweh spoken through Ahijah: the fulfillment of 14:10-11
decisions.reason: Ahijah had told Jeroboam's wife that Yahweh would cut off every male of Jeroboam's house and sweep it away (14:10-11, 14). The narrator notes that the word came true. Baasha's own house will meet the same end for the same sins (16:1-4, 11-12).

decisions.choice: anyone breathing: any living person
decisions.reason: The word for "breath" stands for a living being (Joshua 10:40; 11:11). Jeroboam's whole family was wiped out.

decisions.choice: by the hand of: through
decisions.reason: Yahweh's word was spoken through the prophet as his messenger.

decisions.choice: his servant Ahijah: the prophet as one who serves Yahweh
decisions.reason: "Servant" is a title of honor for those who carry out Yahweh's work, used for Moses and the prophets (2 Kings 17:13, 23). Ahijah had been sent to Jeroboam twice (11:29-39; 14:1-18).

decisions.choice: slave (Literal); servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As for "Moses the servant of the LORD" in these books.

decisions.choice: Baasha; the prophet Ahijah from Shiloh
decisions.reason: Readable names Baasha and says that Ahijah was a prophet; "the Shilonite" means a man from Shiloh.

records.source: עַל־חַטֹּ֤אות יָרָבְעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטָ֔א וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶחֱטִ֖יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל בְּכַעְס֕וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִכְעִ֔יס אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: because of [the] sins of Jeroboam which he sinned and which he caused to sin Israel, by his provocation which he provoked Yahweh God of Israel.
pieces: because of Jeroboam's sins, the sins he had committed and by which he had led Israel to sin, and by which he had provoked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel to anger.

L.30: because of the sins of Jeroboam that he sinned and that he made Israel sin, by his provocation with which he provoked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel.

R.30: It happened because of the sins Jeroboam had committed and by which he had led Israel into sin. He had made {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel angry.

decisions.choice: the sins of Jeroboam which he sinned and caused Israel to sin
decisions.reason: The reason for the end of Jeroboam's house, in the wording of verse 26 and 14:16.

decisions.choice: his provocation which he provoked: his actions that provoked Yahweh to anger
decisions.reason: The noun and verb come from one root meaning to vex or provoke to anger. The words say that Jeroboam's idols were an offense against Yahweh himself (14:9, 15).

decisions.choice: that he sinned and that he made Israel sin / had committed and by which he had led Israel to sin / had committed and by which he had led Israel into sin
decisions.reason: The formula of 14:16 and verse 26, with the plural "sins".

decisions.choice: provoked ... to anger (Balanced); made ... angry (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for this phrase in Kings (14:9, 15): Literal keeps the noun and verb from one root; Balanced says "provoked ... to anger" and Readable "made ... angry" (m2).

records.source: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י נָדָ֖ב וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Nadab and all that he did, [are] not they written on [the] book of [the] matters of the days of [the] kings of Israel?
pieces: The rest of the acts of Nadab, and all that he did, are written in the Book of the History of the Kings of Israel.

L.31: And the rest of the matters of Nadab and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel?

R.31: Everything else Nadab did is written in the history of the kings of Israel.

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel
decisions.reason: The record of the northern kings, as at 14:19; see verse 7.

decisions.choice: a statement in place of the question
decisions.reason: As in verse 7.

records.source: וּמִלְחָמָ֨ה הָיְתָ֜ה בֵּ֣ין אָסָ֗א וּבֵ֛ין בַּעְשָׁ֥א מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כָּל־יְמֵיהֶֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And war was between Asa and between Baasha king of Israel all their days.
pieces: There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel as long as they both lived.

L.32: And there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.

R.32: Asa and Baasha king of Israel were at war with each other as long as they both were king.

decisions.choice: the same words as verse 16
decisions.reason: The sentence repeats verse 16 word for word. Here it leads from the account of Nadab, whom Baasha overthrew, into the account of Baasha's own reign (verses 33-34).

records.source: בִּשְׁנַ֣ת שָׁלֹ֔שׁ לְאָסָ֖א מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָ֠לַךְ בַּעְשָׁ֨א בֶן־אֲחִיָּ֤ה עַל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּתִרְצָ֔ה עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבַּ֖ע שָׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: In [the] year three of Asa king of Judah reigned Baasha son of Ahijah over all Israel in Tirzah, twenty and four years.
pieces: In the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah became king over all Israel in Tirzah, and he reigned twenty-four years.

L.33: In the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah reigned over all Israel in Tirzah, twenty-four years.

R.33: Baasha son of Ahijah became king over all Israel in the third year that Asa was king of Judah. He ruled from Tirzah for twenty-four years.

decisions.choice: reigned ... twenty-four years: became king and reigned twenty-four years
decisions.reason: One verb does both jobs here: it dates the start of the reign and, with the number, gives its length.

decisions.choice: in Tirzah: his capital
decisions.reason: See verse 21.

decisions.choice: and he reigned
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the verb twice, "became king" and "reigned", as the accession formula does at this level.

decisions.choice: the formula of verse 26
decisions.reason: Worded as in verse 26 and 14:16 at each level.
